title: Monsoon fashion guide for men
description: How men should dress for the Indian monsoon: fabrics, shoes, three budget outfits with real brands, and how to protect clothes from damp.
intro: The monsoon ruins the wrong clothes. Denim stays wet. Leather shoes swell. Cotton shirts cling. The fix is simple: quick-dry fabrics, dark or mid colours, shoes that can get wet, and a small umbrella. You do not need a new wardrobe. You need four or five swaps. This guide covers fabrics, shoes, three outfits at three budgets, and the care habits that stop your clothes from smelling.

sections.heading: What fabrics work
sections.body: Choose quick-dry synthetics, nylon blends, and thin cotton blends. Avoid heavy denim, thick cotton, and linen that crumples when wet. Polyester athletic tees dry in an hour and look fine at a casual office. Choose dark and mid colours, like navy, olive, and grey. White and pale colours turn see-through in rain. Skip beige chinos, which show mud and water marks. Look for stretch chinos and nylon pants that dry as you walk.
tips: Wear: quick-dry tees, nylon-blend chinos, thin cotton shirts.
Skip: heavy denim, white trousers, silk, suede.
Colours: navy, olive, charcoal, dark grey.

sections.heading: Footwear that survives
sections.body: Leather shoes and suede do not like water. Pick rubber-soled sneakers, mesh trainers, or sandals like Crocs and Birkenstock-style EVA slides. Keep your good leather pair at the office and commute in the rubber ones. Wear socks that dry fast, or no-show socks in the rain. Dry your shoes with newspaper inside. Never use a hair dryer or direct sun on leather. If your shoes get soaked, stuff them with paper and leave them in a shaded spot.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: Mumbai, Kerala, and the coast get heavy rain from June to September. Delhi, Kolkata, and Chennai have shorter spells and high humidity. In humid weather, sweat does not dry, so pick breathable fabrics. Carry a small umbrella and a spare tee in your bag. Check the forecast the night before. If the day looks wet, wear shorts or cropped trousers to avoid mud on hems.

sections.heading: Looking after your clothes
sections.body: Damp is the real enemy. Dry clothes fully before you store them. Use a dehumidifier or a bag of silica gel in the cupboard. Wash rain-wet clothes the same day, with a drop of vinegar in the rinse for the smell. Store leather shoes with cedar shoe trees or newspaper. Keep a small umbrella and a dry bag at the office. Press clothes before you wear them if the weather has been damp for days.

sections.heading: How to dress for a commute and an office
sections.body: The commute and the office need two different outfits, so pack for both. Wear quick-dry gear and rubber shoes on the road. Keep a dry shirt, a pair of socks, and smart shoes in the office. Change when you arrive. Roll your trousers once if the road is flooded, and roll them back down at your desk. Use a dry bag or a plastic cover inside your backpack for your laptop and your clothes. Take a compact umbrella that fits in a side pocket. A good umbrella is an item you will use for years, so buy the best you can.

sections.heading: What to stop buying
sections.body: Stop buying white trousers for the rainy months. Stop buying new leather shoes in July. Stop buying cheap umbrellas that break in the first wind. Buy one good umbrella and one pair of rubber-sole sneakers.

sections.heading: Grooming in one line
sections.body: Use an anti-frizz hair cream or a short cut, and carry deodorant because humid air makes sweat worse.

faq.q: What should men wear in the monsoon in India?
faq.a: Quick-dry tees, nylon-blend chinos, dark colours, and rubber-sole shoes. Carry a small umbrella and a spare tee.

faq.q: Can I wear jeans in the monsoon?
faq.a: You can, but they stay wet for hours. Choose lighter chinos or stretch pants. If you wear jeans, roll up the hem.

faq.q: What shoes are best for the monsoon?
faq.a: Rubber-sole sneakers, mesh trainers, or EVA slides. Avoid suede and untreated leather.

faq.q: How do I stop clothes smelling in the monsoon?
faq.a: Wash them the same day, dry them fully, and use a dehumidifier or silica gel in the cupboard.
